subject: Onprem TLS: KMS provisioning, DNS mapping and BYOCA CSR options
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice@acme.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: KMS access and DNS mapping for onprem TLS termination

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As discussed, we are evaluating two deployment patterns for Acme's private deployment of Redwood in our VPC: a termination proxy inside our VPC that uses a customer managed KMS key for cert operations, and a CSR-signing flow where our internal CA signs CSRs issued by Redwood. Before we pull the trigger on either path we need concrete answers on the following items so our security and networking teams can sign off: 

- Exact IAM/KMS permissions Redwood needs if we want the proxy to create grants and perform signing operations on our CMK. We have stringent least-privilege requirements.
- If Redwood runs a TLS proxy in our subnet, what DNS entries do you require from us (zone delegation vs individual records)? Do you require the zone to be delegated, or will a per-host CNAME/CERT record suffice for service discovery?
- Impacts to SLA and failure scenarios if we refuse to provide Decrypt permissions and instead opt for an offline signing CA (BYOCA).

Attached is our security questionnaire extract and a short form (acme-kms-access-request.pdf) showing what our infosec team is willing to provide by default.

Can you respond with a short options matrix and a recommended default for enterprise customers who cannot grant broad KMS decrypt access?

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Nguyen
Head of Infrastructure Security, Acme Financial
Attachment: acme-kms-access-request.pdf (pdf stub)

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@acme.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: KMS access and DNS mapping for onprem TLS termination

Alice, thanks for the clear ask and for sending the form. I pulled together the options we typically support and the minimal footprints for each. High level summary first, then specifics.

Short summary (recommended path in bold):
- Option A: Local proxy termination inside your VPC using a customer CMK with a restricted grant pattern. This gives us full control of rotation and OCSP stapling but requires a cross-account CreateGrant and limited Decrypt for the signing path. Good balance for latency and uptime.
- Option B: BYOCA CSR flow where Acme retains signing keys. Redwood pulls CSRs and you deliver signed certs back. This is our recommended default when customers refuse Decrypt permissions because it preserves your key sovereignty. Rotation is still automated on our side but cert issuance is gated on your CA signing cadence.
- Option C: Passthrough SNI with no termination (end-to-end). Minimal Redwood privileges, but we cannot do protocol-level features like response shaping, streaming cache, or OCSP stapling. Acceptable for strict key control but worse for observability and performance.

Permissions and KMS notes (Option A):
- Minimum grants we ask for: kms:CreateGrant, kms:DescribeKey, kms:RetireGrant on a per-session principal; and a narrowly scoped kms:Sign or kms:Decrypt depending on the KMS key type (asymmetric vs symmetric).
- We do not require kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion or key rotation rights. We require the ability to create ephemeral grants with time limits and single-use cryptographic operations.
- For CloudHSM or on-prem HSMs where KMS style grants are not supported, we recommend an agent-based offline signer (see Option B).

DNS mapping requirements:
- If you can delegate a subzone (example: redwood.acme.internal) to Redwood managed name servers inside your VPC, that is the simplest model for scale and multi-tenant routing.
- If delegation is not acceptable, we can operate with explicit per-host A/CNAME entries. Minimum required records: one CNAME (or A) per endpoint plus an SRV record if you want port-based discovery. For mutual-TLS client mapping you may also need a TXT record registering the expected SAN policy.

SLA and failure modes (brief):
- Option A (proxy + CMK): normal SLA. If KMS grant creation fails (permissions revoked) we will failover to a short-lived Redwood-managed cert (TTL ~24 hours) if you accept a temporary exception; otherwise the endpoint will become degraded.
- Option B (BYOCA): SLA depends on your CA signing turn-around. We can automate polling and certificate replacement but if your CA team delays signing we will mark endpoints as degraded and follow the SLA exception runbook.

Action items I propose:
1) Security-only sync (30m) to agree exact IAM grant scoping and acceptable key operations.
2) Networking sync (30m) to pick zone-delegation vs per-host record model.
3) Technical handoff doc and JIRA runbook entry (I have created JIRA-INF-1243 and will attach our cert-rotation template).

If this sounds right, we can schedule the two syncs this week. I will loop in an engineer for a short demo of our CSR puller flow.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: KMS access and DNS mapping for onprem TLS termination — rotation notes

Looping in a couple operational constraints from SRE side:

- Rotation cadence: we recommend 60-90 day certs for short-lived certs and automated renewal. With BYOCA the cadence is subject to your CA policy; we can accept 180 day certs but will flag longer TTLs in monitoring.
- Audit and evidence: we can push signed audit proofs and CSR bundles to a customer-owned S3 bucket or to your on-prem object storage. If you require HSM-backed signing with no external write, Option B with an offline signer is the best fit.
- Key escrow and emergency access: we do not keep copies of private keys for BYOCA flows. For Option A we use ephemeral grants only; your security team can inspect grant logs.

I attached a quick flow diagram for the rotation and failover path. It shows the automated fallback to a Redwood-managed short-lived cert only if you authorize that exception in your change request.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Platform Ops, Redwood Inference
Attachment: cert-rotation-flow.png (image stub)

From: Bob Lang <bob@acme.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 15:01:00 -0800
Subject: Re: KMS access and DNS mapping for onprem TLS termination

Thanks Priyom and Marissa,

A couple clarifications from our security team after reviewing your options:
- We cannot grant Decrypt or Sign permissions to any external tenant. We can provide an asymmetric CMK that only supports Sign operations under our control or an offline CA that will sign CSRs on demand.
- Zone delegation is out of scope for Acme internal DNS. We will only provide per-host records.

Given that, can you confirm whether the CSR puller flow will fully support the following?
1) Redwood generates CSR and places it into a signed request bundle.
2) Acme CA team receives the bundle via secure S3 or internal pipeline and returns a signed cert bundle.
3) Redwood ingests the signed cert and rotates certs without human intervention thereafter.

Second question: if we go BYOCA CSR flow, what is the behavior when our CA team is delayed? Do you have an outage mitigation plan that preserves connectivity (even in reduced functionality) to meet our app SLA?

Thanks,
Bob
Infrastructure Engineer, Acme Financial

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: KMS access and DNS mapping for onprem TLS termination

Bob — good questions, and yes we support the CSR puller flow end-to-end. Concrete behavior and mitigations below.

CSR puller flow (Option B) detailed steps:
- Redwood generates keys and CSR inside the runtime that is either: (a) a proxy container you host in your VPC or (b) a Redwood-managed runtime with the private key held in-memory only.
- CSR is packaged with metadata (requested SANs, validity window, rotation intent) and uploaded to a customer-controlled secure endpoint (S3 bucket with write-only uploads or an approved API endpoint).
- Your CA team signs and returns the certificate bundle to the same endpoint. Redwood polls the endpoint and performs an automated import and replacement when a new signed bundle is available.

Mitigation if Acme CA team is delayed: 
- Option 1 (preferred): You authorize a pre-approved emergency exception in a change request. On detection of a signer delay (configurable threshold, default 4 hours), Redwood will automatically failover to a short-lived Redwood-managed cert (24 hour TTL). This preserves TLS connectivity while keeping the impact window small. Use of this emergency cert is recorded in audit logs and requires your explicit approval in the initial provisioning request.
- Option 2: If you do not permit emergency exceptions, Redwood will mark endpoints as degraded and generate alerts and a runbook for manual intervention. In that case continuity depends entirely on your CA team's response time.

Operational notes:
- We support secure S3-based exchange and direct SFTP or API push. For high-security environments we can also support a signed bundle drop to your on-prem object storage via an SCP agent.
- We provide hooks to emit audit evidence into your SIEM via our agent or push to a customer-owned S3.

Next steps:
1) If you prefer BYOCA, please confirm which exchange mechanism you prefer (secure S3 write-only prefix, SFTP endpoint, or in-band API).
2) Please indicate whether you will accept a pre-approved emergency exception for a Redwood-managed short-lived cert and the maximum allowed TTL for that fallback.

I will add the technical runbook link to JIRA-INF-1243. We can also do a 30m handoff with your CA team.

Thanks,
Priyom

Priyom and team,

Thanks for the thorough explanations. After internal review Acme will proceed with the BYOCA CSR puller flow and will not grant Decrypt permissions. We will: 

- Provide a secure S3 prefix (write-only for Redwood) where CSRs will be dropped and signed certs uploaded.
- Accept Redwood polling cadence and automated import but we will not allow any automatic Redwood-managed fallback certs. Instead, in an emergency we will trigger a documented change that allows a short-lived fallback; that process will be defined during the handoff call.

Please schedule the security and network handoff next week. Our CA team will join and Bob will be the primary contact. I attached our signed exception request for the handoff scheduling.

Alice
